title: instruction-skein-tinker-log
summary: Personal experiment log for trying combinatorial prompt templates and compact few-shot exemplars. Includes quick failure triage, token budget notes, and candidate fallback patterns to feed into the internal prompt library.
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick, portable notes to capture small experiments for the user-facing prompt library. Not meant to be canonical yet; this is where I try awkward/contrarian ideas.
- Focus: compact few-shot exemplars that hit both correctness and token-efficiency for short assistant responses (<= 120 tokens generated).
- Audience: me + DX folks (Jon, Priya) to surface winners to the prompt registry.

Top-level hypotheses I'm testing:
1) Short, annotated exemplars (1-2 lines) produce more consistent formatting than long narrative examples when using instruction-tuned opensource models.
2) Explicit negative exemplars ("bad_output") reduce hallucinations for fact-synthesis tasks more than adding more positive examples.
3) Minimal role framing + a constrained output schema yields lower token use while preserving quality for short answers.

Experiment 1: compact few-shot rotation (3-shot, single-line exemplars)
- Template: 
  System: You are a concise assistant. Return only the JSON object requested.
  User: Task + question
  Examples (few-shot): three lines each: input => {"answer": "..."} 
- Shots (examples):
  1) "Define: latency. => {"answer": "time taken for model to return tokens"}"
  2) "Define: throughput. => {"answer": "tokens processed per second"}"
  3) "Define: KV cache. => {"answer": "a temporary store for past key/value attention states"}"
- Observations: shorter exemplars forced the model to stick to JSON but occasionally used synonyms ("temporary buffer") which is acceptable. 3-shot seemed sweet spot. 1-shot too brittle, 5-shot increased tokens without much gain.
- Token budget: exemplar block ~160 tokens; prompt total w/ user ~220 tokens. Generated output average ~18 tokens.
- Next: try replacing one positive with a negative exemplar.

Experiment 2: negative exemplar injection
- Change: second shot becomes a negative example: 
  "Define: throughput. => BAD_OUTPUT: "throughput is how fast the cloud works""
- Rationale: show explicit wrong pattern to discourage vague/buzzwordy replies.
- Observations: model sometimes echoes the phrase "avoid: ..." which leaks into output. To mitigate, use a wrapper: 
  Example: GOOD => {..}, BAD => [bad_ex1] and in system say "Do NOT produce BAD outputs".
- Outcome: small improvement on avoiding vague buzzwords, but sometimes the model produced a paraphrase of the bad example rather than negating it. So it's inconsistent.

Experiment 3: constrained schema + role minimalism
- Template:
  System: You are a strict formatter. Return exactly {"label": <one-word>, "explanation": <one-sentence>} and nothing else.
  Few-shot: 2 examples.
- Tasks: micro-definitions, triage labels ("OK", "AMBIG", "INVALID").
- Observed: model follows schema strictly for small models fine; for larger models it sometimes adds trailing punctuation or commentary. Adding an explicit token limit in system helped ("<=20 tokens").

Failure cases catalog (short list)
- Hallucinated references when asked "cite a source" for short synthesis. Model fabricates plausible-looking URLs.
- Overly literal negative examples leading to repeated bad phrasing.
- Schema drift when the user query is long: model ignores schema and returns a paragraph.
- Tokens creeping above 120 due to verbose synonyms and disclaimers.

Quick mitigations to try next
- Add a hard "format check" step in prompt: "If you deviate, output ERROR_FORMAT and stop." (test for both Llama2-70B and open models we host).
- Move negative examples into a separate "do_not" list and reference it via a single-line pointer in system.
- Use a trailing guard token sequence: "###END_JSON###" and instruct model to close JSON before that.

Candidate prompt variants to promote into the registry (shortlist)
- variant_a_compact-json-2shot: minimal system + 2 one-line exemplars; explicit token cap.
- variant_b_badlist-pointer: use a separate BAD list and a single positive exemplar.
- variant_c_schema-guard: include trailing guard token and explicit ERROR_FORMAT instruction.

Scratch outputs (copied raw from model runs)
- Input (variant_a_compact-json-2shot): 
  "System: You are concise. Return only {"label": <one word>, "explanation": <one sentence>}. Max gen tokens 20.
   User: Is dynamic batching useful?"
- Model: {"label":"YES","explanation":"reduces per-token cost by grouping requests"}
- Input (variant_b_badlist-pointer): same task but BAD list includes "batching is only for training"
- Model: {"label":"YES","explanation":"groups inference requests to reduce overhead"}  // good
- Failure raw: user asked "give a source" -> model: {"label":"YES","explanation":"see https://journal.ai/tech/fast-batching"}  // fabricated link

Notes-to-self / TODOs
- Automate a tiny harness to evaluate schema compliance over 500 samples (Jon to help JIRA DX-4123).
- Try these variants across model families: redwood-hosted-7b, redwood-hosted-13b-int8, local-llama2-70b. Capture top-3 failure types and tokens.
- Add a small check in the prompt library UI to show "token delta" estimates for each exemplar set.
- Consider a micro A/B rollout in console: track schema compliance and user-facing error count.

Open questions
- Do negative examples generalize across intents, or only the exact phrasing? So far looks phrasing-sensitive.
- Is there a better way to show "bad" outputs without priming the same wording? Maybe use abstractive labels instead of quoting the bad sentence.

Slack threads / references
- #dx-prompt-tests: thread id 2389 (contains raw run dumps)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-kits#88 (draft transformer for variant metadata)

Appendix: candidate micro-bench harness sketch (manual steps)
1) Select 200 seed user prompts from real product telemetry (short Q/A, <=40 tokens).
2) For each candidate variant, run through three model sizes and record: generated tokens, schema_ok (binary), hallucination_flag (heuristic: presence of "http" or "www" in output).
3) Export CSV and compute pass rate.
4) Promote variant if schema_ok >= 0.95 and hallucination_flag <= 0.02 and median generated tokens <= 40.

End notes:
- This file will probably be split into a proper PRD if we get a promising winner. For now, iterative, messy, and intentionally terse.
- If you want to run a quick check, ping me on Slack or add a note in JIRA DX-4123.
